facts.text: ISO/TC 127 is the ISO technical committee for earth-moving machinery; the numbers, parts and years in a standard's name identify the document and edition.
facts.quote: ISO/TC 127 is the ISO committee for earth-moving machinery, and the numbers, parts and years in a standard's name tell you exactly which document and which edition is meant.

facts.text: Nearly every off-road standard covered by the booklet comes from ISO/TC 127: ISO 21815 for collision systems, ISO 16001 for object detection, ISO 3450 for brakes, ISO 19014 for functional safety, ISO 17757 for autonomous machines and ISO 6165 for machine definitions.
facts.quote: nearly every off-road standard in the booklet comes from it: the ISO 21815 collision series, ISO 16001 on object detection, ISO 3450 on brakes, ISO 19014 on functional safety, ISO 17757 on autonomous machines and ISO 6165, which defines the machines [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The booklet found no ISO/TC 127 study on applying road-vehicle simulation methods to off-road machines.
facts.quote: The booklet found no ISO/TC 127 study on applying road-vehicle simulation methods to off-road machines [Chapter 2].

facts.text: In ISO 21815-1:2022, ISO identifies the standards body, 21815 is the standard number, -1 identifies Part 1 and 2022 is the edition year; each part of a multi-part series is a separate document with its own scope and date.
facts.quote: In "ISO 21815-1:2022", "ISO" is the body, "21815" the standard's number, "-1" Part 1 of a multi-part series (each part is a separate document with its own scope and date) and ":2022" the edition year.

facts.text: ISO 16001:2017 is a single-part standard whose current edition is from 2017.
facts.quote: "ISO 16001:2017" is a single-part standard whose current edition is from 2017

facts.text: An old edition year does not necessarily mean a standard is outdated: ISO 3450:2011 was reviewed and confirmed in 2022.
facts.quote: an old year does not mean an outdated text, since ISO 3450:2011 was reviewed and confirmed in 2022 [Chapter 8].

facts.text: A new edition of an ISO standard replaces the old edition; all five parts of ISO 19014 change in October 2026.
facts.quote: A new edition replaces the old one, which is why the booklet keeps saying that all five parts of ISO 19014 change in October 2026 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: ISO document prefixes identify document types: ISO/TS means technical specification, ISO/PAS means publicly available specification, ISO/IEC TR means a technical report written jointly with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), and ISO/PRF means a standard at proof stage.
facts.quote: "ISO/TS" a technical specification, "ISO/PAS" a publicly available specification, "ISO/IEC TR" a technical report written jointly with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC), "ISO/PRF" a standard at proof stage.

facts.text: The prefix EN ISO marks a European adoption of a standard, while AS marks an Australian adoption.
facts.quote: Prefixes such as "EN ISO" or "AS" mark a European or Australian adoption.

facts.text: Mixing standard editions is a risk for the off-road collision-mitigation program; the plan should baseline the ISO 19014 editions actually published in October 2026 rather than mix clauses from 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2026.
facts.quote: Mixing editions is a real risk. The plan should baseline the ISO 19014 editions actually published in October 2026 rather than mixing 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2026 clauses

facts.text: ISO 21815-4 should not be cited as published until its text appears.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-4 should not be cited as published until its text appears [Chapter 3].
